correctness.rationale: For every n>=3 and nonempty S the proof explicitly reduces graph-state entropy to binary cross-cut rank, gives a ring automorphism establishing rank in the linear-term cases, reduces the odd full parity case via even-translation group algebra to a square-zero tensor differential and computes its homology. This derives the full eigenvalue list with correct normalization and boundaries; 1030 independent finite GF2 checks and six direct quantum partial traces corroborate but do not replace it. Exact package checker path verify.py and recorded output verification_output.txt are included.

originality.rationale: The exact all-coordinate-parity Schmidt spectrum for antipodally augmented hypercube graph states, with the odd-dimensional full-parity dyadic correction and macroscopic entanglement loss after adding the antipodal matching, was not found as a statement or implied corollary in inspected primary sources or related published records. The general graph-state cut-rank theorem (Hein et al.) and earlier ordinary-hypercube graph-state instances (Hashizume et al.) are explicitly prior methods and are not claimed. Real-spectrum folded-cube results and free-fermion entanglement concern different invariants/states. Specialized historical binary adjacency-rank work remains a priority risk.
residual_risks: An older specialized theorem giving binary adjacency rank of folded hypercubes, related group-algebra ideals, or their symmetric cut-rank functions could imply the new formula and alter priority.

value.rationale: A single natural nonlocal perfect matching systematically destroys half-system maximal entanglement on a family of structured parity cuts; the exact exceptional n-odd full-parity correction arises from a nontrivial tensor-differential homology invariant. The full flat spectrum is calculated uniformly for all finite n and all nonempty S, offering sharp network-entanglement benchmarks and a structurally motivated boundary phenomenon.
